title: And Is There, Lord, a Rest
description: And Is There, Lord, a Rest in Tonic Solfa to BOYLSTON, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Ray Palmer wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 563 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Heavenly Rest”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to BOYLSTON; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: And is there, Lord, a rest, For wea-ry souls de-signed, Where not a care shall stir the breast, Or sor-row en-trance find?

lines: And is there, Lord, a rest,
Where not a care shall stir the breast,
And live and love, nor ever roam
Then let me, gracious God, ascend

licence: Public domain: Ray Palmer died in 1887.
credits: Words by Ray Palmer (1808–1887), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to BOYLSTON by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
